tokens.name: duck-yellow
tokens.usage: The brand colour (DuckDB yellow-50). Fills only: the mark, primary buttons, the match highlight in dark UIs, cover blocks. Never text or thin lines on `surface` in light (1.15:1). Text on it is `on-yellow`.

tokens.name: duck-yellow-hover
tokens.usage: Hover and pressed fill for anything painted `duck-yellow` (DuckDB yellow-45). Text on it is `on-yellow` (13.8:1).

tokens.name: on-yellow
tokens.usage: Text, icons and the mark's eye on `duck-yellow` and `duck-yellow-hover` in both themes (16.5:1).

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Page background for the website and docs (DuckDB grey-99 / grey-05).

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Cards, nav bar, popovers sitting on `surface`. Separate from `surface` with a `border` hairline, not a shadow.

tokens.name: surface-code
tokens.usage: Terminal and code-block background (DuckDB CLI background). Syntax tokens `code-*` are checked on this ground.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and headings on `surface`, `surface-raised` and `surface-code` (≥16.4:1 in both themes). Also the fill of the ink mark.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text: captions, metadata, line numbers, placeholders, on `surface`, `surface-raised` and `surface-code` (≥5.3:1 in both themes).

tokens.name: border
tokens.usage: Decorative hairlines: card outlines, table rules, section dividers. Not for control edges (below 3:1).

tokens.name: border-strong
tokens.usage: Edges of inputs, secondary buttons and checkboxes: ≥3.8:1 on `surface` in both themes.

tokens.name: link
tokens.usage: Inline links on `surface` and `surface-raised` (DuckDB yellow-20 / yellow-50; 6.5:1 light, 16.5:1 dark). Underline on hover.

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: Focus ring: 2px solid, 2px offset, on every interactive element (5.2:1 light, 9.9:1 dark on `surface`). Blue so it never reads as a yellow match.

tokens.name: match-bg
tokens.usage: Background of the matched span in duckgrep query output and site search results; the brand's signature highlight. Text on it is `match-ink`.

tokens.name: match-ink
tokens.usage: Text of a matched span on `match-bg` (16.5:1 light, 9.4:1 dark).

tokens.name: accent-orange
tokens.usage: Secondary brand hue (DuckDB orange-50), used sparingly: a 'new' tag, cover blocks, one chart series. Fill only; text on it is `on-yellow` (6.7:1). Never body text.

tokens.name: code-keyword
tokens.usage: SQL keywords and path columns in duckgrep output, on `surface-code` (4.8:1 light, 8:1 dark). From the DuckDB CLI palette.

tokens.name: code-string
tokens.usage: String literals on `surface-code` (5.4:1 light, 13.1:1 dark). From the DuckDB CLI palette.

tokens.name: code-number
tokens.usage: Numeric literals on `surface-code` (5.6:1 light, 5.9:1 dark). Light value darkened from DuckDB's #d700af, which is 4.35:1 here.

tokens.name: code-function
tokens.usage: Function names and line numbers of hits on `surface-code` (5.2:1 light, 6.3:1 dark). Light value darkened from DuckDB's #008700 (4.39:1).

tokens.name: code-comment
tokens.usage: Comments and the shell prompt `$` on `surface-code` (5.7:1 light, 5.2:1 dark).

tokens.name: code-error
tokens.usage: Errors on `surface-code` (5:1 light, 6.6:1 dark). Always paired with the word 'error', never colour alone.

styles.name: display
styles.sample: Grep finds strings. duckgrep answers questions.

styles.name: h3
styles.sample: It joins code with its history.

styles.name: body-lg
styles.sample: Give your coding agent a live, queryable model of your codebase (definitions, callers, imports, history), so structural questions take one query instead of a search loop.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Coding agents find their way around a codebase with chains of grep → read file → grep again. That works for “where is this string.”

styles.usage: Terminal blocks, code blocks, inline code.

styles.usage: Eyebrows and tags, set in capitals.
